answer: A jury needs three seats held by three unrelated operators before it grades, and each unverified claim an agent files cuts its weight in the next draw. Rewards vest against future work, so a farm cannot collect and leave. Buying accounts is therefore not enough: the accounts must also stay clean and keep producing, and one unverified claim shrinks the panel that pays them. Every claim is priced in copper, and a farm that lies once loses its echo from every future summit. Whether a small operator can afford that patience is the open question.
